Carlos Lehder on Partnering with Boston George to Traffick Cocaine in America (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/AxHbPY_r1q4
--------
In this VladTV segment, Carlos Lehder recounts how his relationship with “Boston George” Jung grew from a prison connection into a cocaine trafficking operation targeting the United States in the mid-1970s. Lehder says George used furloughs to Massachusetts to move copies of his federal sentence and indictment to contacts in California, helping convince financiers that a Colombian smuggler could supply a market paying up to $70,000 per kilo. Boston George also describes learning the value of cocaine while flying out of Mexico and realizing he could build a route into America.

Lehder explains how profits were tied to cars bought in the U.S., shipped to Medellín, Colombia, and sold through his dealership, Later Autos. He also details how that business led him to meet Pablo Escobar’s cousin, who eventually introduced him to Escobar himself.

recentItems.title: Vlad Tenev on Being Worth $2 Billion at Age 34 When Robinhood Went Public (Part 8)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 7: https://youtu.be/eDnOaXKnuFY
Part 1: https://youtu.be/8YYmtZYQ0Aw
--------
Robinhood co-founder Vlad Tenev sits down with DJ Vlad to reflect on the company’s July 29, 2021 Nasdaq IPO under the ticker HOOD, following the GameStop trading controversy and the peak of the meme stock era. Tenev explains why the symbol “HOOD” fit the brand, how Robinhood reached a $32 billion valuation, and what it felt like to see his net worth estimated at $2.1 billion at just 34 years old.

Instead of describing the moment as a victory lap, Tenev says IPO day was stressful and “one of the worst” days of his life. He details the COVID-era process: Zoom roadshows from JPMorgan’s New York offices, a rapidly growing remote team, masked crowds in Manhattan, and the pressure of watching Robinhood shares drop on opening day.

A candid look at wealth, public markets, startup pressure, and the reality behind a high-profile fintech debut.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/WLjwcVFanlw
--------
In this VladTV segment, Memo600 reflects on the complicated personal ties behind Chicago drill history, recalling Chief Keef’s cousin Big Glo, also known as Blood Money, and his early role in the Glory Boyz/Glo Gang movement after Keef’s Interscope deal. Memo shares memories of buying his first firearm from Big Glo and revisits the optimism surrounding Glo before his death.

The conversation then turns to RondoNumbaNine and Cdai’s murder conviction in the killing of cab driver Javon Boyd, whom Memo reveals was his blood cousin. Memo discusses the painful reality of having close friends convicted in a case involving his own family, while honoring Boyd’s memory and offering condolences. Vlad also connects the discussion to interviews with Robert O’Neill and Nicholas Irving, touching on weapons, street survival, and the lasting impact of violence in Chicago’s rap scene.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/gKnZIQpWXOc
--------
After serving 28 years in prison, Vincent Marino sits down with VladTV to discuss life after his RICO case, why he says he will never return to crime, and his move into writing and filmmaking. Marino talks about his book *Patriarca Purge*, available through Marino Entertainment LLC, plans for a TV miniseries inspired by *The Sopranos* and *Animal Kingdom*, and his upcoming film *Pressed* with director Rex Palmer.

The conversation also turns to the modern Patriarca crime family, including the Boston faction, late reputed leader Carmen “The Cheese Man” DiNunzio, and Robert “Bobby” Russo, whom Marino says was his co-defendant and is now allegedly linked to leadership of the family. Marino reflects on how organized crime has changed since the violent 1990s, while discussing Boston’s North End, the FBI, the Department of Justice, and his future projects with Nicole Barsky.

--------
Poetik Flakko and DJ Vlad break down hip-hop’s shifting definition of “bigger” and “more impactful,” debating Future’s cultural influence versus J. Cole’s conscious rap legacy. Vlad revisits the era when Public Enemy, Chuck D, Flavor Flav and the Bomb Squad pushed politically charged music to the top with classics like *It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back*, *Fear of a Black Planet* and “Fight the Power,” even influencing Ice Cube’s *AmeriKKKa’s Most Wanted*. The discussion turns to today’s biggest rap names — Kendrick Lamar, Drake, J. Cole and Future — before Spotify monthly listener numbers challenge assumptions and support Flakko’s argument about Future’s reach. Flakko also addresses rap’s impact on drug culture, street violence, South Central, inner-city communities and the divide between everyday civilians and the small percentage driving crime in neighborhoods across America.

recentItems.title: William Noguera on Getting Arrested at 19 for Murder & Becoming a Sureño in Jail (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/W6Vqal8IQfk
--------
In this VladTV interview, William Noguera revisits the 1983 murder case that changed his life, explaining how investigators built a first-degree murder charge with a special circumstance of financial gain despite limited physical evidence, no DNA, and no fingerprints. Noguera discusses the witness claims, the alleged insurance-money motive, and the emotional spiral he says followed the killing, including car theft, fighting, and guilt over failing to protect his child.

Arrested at 19 and held without bond, Noguera spent four years in Orange County Jail awaiting trial. He details how jail politics shaped his survival, describing Southern Mexican gang influence, Sureño affiliation, Mexican Mafia associates, tier tender duties, and learning how “the car” operated behind bars. The conversation offers a firsthand look at California jail culture, gang structure, and the legal realities of a major murder case before the modern DNA era and the O.J. Simpson trial spotlighted forensic evidence.
